newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Alleged "British spy" suffers Moscow court setback.
newsitem.headline: Alleged "British spy" suffers Moscow court setback.

text.p: Russian judges reviewing the case of a junior foreign ministry official alleged to have spied for Britain declined to accept documents attesting he was not mentally fit to stand trial, his lawyer said on Tuesday.
"They refused to satisfy the request," said lawyer Anatoly Kucherena, who is representing Platon Obukhov, 28.
Kucherena is hoping that criminal proceedings in a Moscow City Court could be dropped if the court decides Obukhov is unfit.

The judges meeting behind closed doors also listened to the testimony of an doctor who examined Obukov, he said, but added they rejected an appeal that Obukhov's parents be appointed his legal guardians.
A second secretary in the Foreign Ministry's prestigious North America Department, Obukhov has been held since April, 1996, on charges he was paid for information by British MI6 agents.
Obukhov's lawyer and his parents insist he has been mentally unstable since childhood and is unfit to stand trial. They want him discharged to a psychiatric hospital.
"Platon Obukhov's condition today is such that he cannot attend the court sessions," Kucherena told reporters. "His incoherent behavior and the worsening of his health doesn't allow him to attend."
If the court rules Obukhov was sane at the time of the alleged crime and is capable in principle of facing charges, he will be admitted to hospital and tried when he recovers.
